why.terrace: No known organised supporters' group; crowds often a few hundred.
why.city: Gibraltar's dominant club, but a small territory where football is a minor pastime.
why.voice: No documented supporter ownership or influence (estimate).
why.conscience: Nothing notable found; little visible inclusion work (estimate).
why.ground: Shares the 2,000-seat Victoria Stadium with every Gibraltar club; small crowds.
why.contender: 30 Gibraltar titles incl. six straight (2021-2026); Rock Cup 2026.
why.rituals: No traditions known beyond the club.
why.stewardship: Run by a club board under president Dylan Viagas; no outside investor reported (estimate).
why.women: Women's team in the Gibraltar Women's League, a small competition.
why.intensity: Dominant at home, outmatched in Europe; mixed (estimate).

why.terrace: No known supporters' group; modern club (founded 2015) with small crowds (estimate).
why.city: A 2015 creation in a city with several clubs and little football following.
why.voice: Privately controlled company (SIA); no supporter role.
why.conscience: Nothing notable found; no visible inclusion work (estimate).
why.ground: Skonto Stadium (8,087), largely empty for league matches (estimate).
why.stewardship: Linked to Russian billionaire Sergey Lomakin (Fix Price), who also backs Pafos; ownership opaque, chairman Aleksandrs Pronins.
why.women: Women's team founded 2024, Latvian champions twice; small league.

why.terrace: No known supporters' group (formerly Saburtalo, a youth-focused club) (estimate).
why.city: Tbilisi district club; Dinamo Tbilisi is the city's main team.
why.voice: Owned by a business group; no supporter role.
why.conscience: Nothing notable found; no visible inclusion work (estimate).
why.ground: Mikheil Meskhi Stadium (27,223), far too big for its crowds (estimate).
why.stewardship: Iberia Business Group of Tariel Khechikashvili (former sports minister), owner since 2005; private, not state.

why.terrace: A small, newly developing fan base; no known ultras group (estimate).
why.city: Kaunas's main football club, but the city lives through basketball (Zalgiris BC).
why.voice: Privately owned; no supporter role found.
why.conscience: Nothing notable found; no visible inclusion work (estimate).
why.ground: Darius and Girenas Stadium (15,026, renovated 2022), largest in the Baltics; crowds far below capacity (estimate).
why.contender: First Lithuanian title 2025; LFF Cup 2026; regular top three since 2020.
why.stewardship: Local owners: Paulius Motiejunas (70%) and basketball great Mantas Kalnietis (30%, chairman).

why.terrace: Supporters' club Sillastrybarna, with tifo displays; small but organised.
why.city: The pride of Hälleviks fishing village (about 800 people) and Sölvesborg; 2025 title squad mostly local-born.
why.voice: Swedish member association under the 51% rule; members elect the board.
why.conscience: Nothing notable found; standard Swedish community work (estimate).
why.ground: Strandvallen (about 6,750) by the sea, near full for big matches (5,000-6,000 in 2025).
why.contender: First Allsvenskan title 2025 and Svenska Cupen 2025-26; before that a mid-table club.
why.rituals: Herring ('sill') identity and seaside ground known in Sweden.
why.stewardship: Member-owned non-profit association; chairman Jan Sjöblom.
why.intensity: Well-organised, resilient side, aggressive in the title season; mixed.

why.terrace: No organised support beyond a few followers (estimate).
why.city: Club of Escaldes-Engordany in Andorra, where football draws very small crowds.
why.ground: No ground of its own; plays at federation stadiums.
why.contender: Five Andorran titles (incl. 2025, 2026) and three cups since 2020; first Andorran club in a European league phase.
why.stewardship: Private club, backed early by builder Construccions Modernes; chairman Pablo Gomez (estimate).

why.terrace: Lesinari (Vultures, founded 1987), oldest organised group in Bosanska Krajina, loud north stand.
why.city: Banja Luka's main club and a symbol of the city and Republika Srpska.
why.voice: No documented supporter role in decisions (estimate).
why.conscience: Fans repeatedly glorify war criminal Ratko Mladic (2025-26 chants, 2026 Lesinari banner); RFE/RL reports a UEFA fine for racist fan behaviour; victims' groups filed a UEFA complaint (Sept 2026).
why.ground: Banja Luka City Stadium (10,030), sold out for big European nights.
why.contender: Bosnian champions 2011, 2021, 2024, 2026; Conference League last 16 in 2024-25.
why.rituals: Lesinari choreos known in the Balkans; little beyond.
why.stewardship: President Zvjezdan Misimovic; depends on city and regional public funding (estimate, ownership unclear; not a sovereign state owner).

why.terrace: Small home following; no known organised group (estimate).
why.city: The only club of the small town of Rrogozhine, which part-owns it.
why.conscience: UEFA fined the club EUR 10,000 with a suspended closure for fans' discriminatory chants v Borac Banja Luka (2024 Champions League qualifier).
why.stewardship: Italian-based construction firms Demrozi Costruzioni and Foglia Engineering (37.5% each) plus Rrogozhine municipality (25%); president Agim Demrozi.

why.terrace: Small support; no known organised group of note (estimate).
why.city: Paphos's main club, but a 2014 merger with shallow roots.
why.conscience: Nothing notable found; no visible inclusion work (estimate).
why.ground: Stelios Kyriakides Stadium (about 9,300); European matches moved to Limassol's Alphamega Stadium.
why.contender: Cypriot champions 2025, cups 2024 and 2026; Champions League league phase 2025-26.
why.stewardship: Russian billionaire Sergey Lomakin (Fix Price) with chairman Roman Dubov via Total Sports Investments; part of a loose network with Riga FC.
